http/websocket_client#

Opening a WebSocket connection as a client.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let connection = await WebSocketConnecting(url: ParsedUrl("wss://example.com/chat").parts()).connection();
await connection.send_text("hello");
let reply = await connection.message();

Description#

Opening a WebSocket connection as a client.

Like HttpClient(), it resolves with the system's DNS, trusts the system's roots and reaches public endpoints only; WebSocketPolicy changes that and the timeouts (30 seconds to open, 5 to close).

object WebSocketConnecting#

object WebSocketConnecting

Direct HTTP1 Upgrade opener; ordinary Exchanging cannot transfer the socket. Repeated connection() observes the same lazy attempt/result, never reconnects.

WebSocketConnecting.WebSocketConnecting#

WebSocketConnecting(url is UrlParts, protocols is @string = [], headers is Headers = Headers(), resolver is Resolving = SystemResolution(), trust is TrustStore = SystemTrustStore(), policy is WebSocketPolicy = WebSocketPolicy(), clock is Timing = SystemClock())

WebSocketConnecting(url: ParsedUrl("wss://example.com/chat").parts()): the system's DNS and trusted roots, no subprotocols and no extra headers unless given, as HttpClient() does.

WebSocketConnecting.WebSocketConnecting#

WebSocketConnecting(url is UrlParts, protocols is @string, headers is Headers, resolver is Resolving, tls is TlsClientPolicy, policy is WebSocketPolicy, clock is Timing)

The same with an explicit TLS policy.

WebSocketConnecting.connection#

async connection() is WebSocketConnection

Connects once and gives the connection; later calls give the same one.
